title: Fibonacci-partition power sums have algebraic growth exponents whose exponential scale tends to the square root of the golden ratio
author: Carlo Sanna
difficulty_reason: The argument constructs a synchronized product automaton for arbitrary integer moments and explicitly classifies its reachable states to obtain primitive Perron-Frobenius growth. It then controls the inaccessible spectral blocks and reduces arbitrary binary matrix products to two-dimensional factors with sharp spectral-norm bounds. These local constructions identify the generalized spectral radius, allowing a Kronecker-power limit theorem to determine the asymptotic moment exponent.
source_version: Discrete Analysis 2025:2, 13 pp.; DOI 10.19086/da.137601; publisher-linked version of record arXiv:2309.12724v2 (3 May 2025)

proof_review.method: Read complete Theorems1.1–1.2 and Sections2–4 in pinned publisher-linked original PDF
proof_review.note: One combined unit preserves shared moment automaton and its spectral-radius construction; no separate counting of exponents, spectral-radius helper or parameter values. Power sums are comparable up to p-dependent constants, not a full asymptotic equivalent for all integer N. Counts distinct strictly increasing Fibonacci terms with f1=1,f2=2; positive integer p. Berstel automaton, Zeckendorf uniqueness, Perron-Frobenius automaton theorem, Blondel–Nesterov nonnegative Kronecker-power limit and Berger–Wang equality are named prerequisites. All new reachable-state classification, inaccessible triangular blocks and binary-product spectral control is printed. Finite transition checks (t1–t10) are bounded checks from the displayed four-state automaton; spectral-norm values h=2–7 are explicitly bounded finite2×2 matrix checks. No omitted new core.
